chunks: My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from ‘Abdil Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, who said:

I asked Abā Ja’far (peace be upon him), “What is the reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) with the (sole) intention of Ziyārah?” He replied, “(Their reward is) Paradise and the reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Abil Ḥasan (peace be upon him) is (also) Paradise.”
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Kazim?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the theological significance of the Imams' graves as intercessory sites, specifically highlighting Imam al-Kāẓim’s status in Baghdad. It reflects the Shia tradition of linking physical visitation with spiritual elevation, positioning the Imams as direct conduits to Paradise alongside the Prophet.
